newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate leaps 80 bps to 9.1 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate leaps 80 bps to 9.1 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average money market rate leapt 80 basis points to 9.1 percent on Wednesday, boosted by strong interbank borrowing at higher rates.
Total settlements were halved to 12 million kuna, of which nine were new loans. Supply rose to 65 million, but dealers said creditors could not match demand for longer-term funds.
The rates were unchanged, ranging between 8.0 percent for call money and 12 percent on 31-366 day funds.
Insurers' five-10 loans were rolled over at seven percent.
Due to very weak demand by banks with shortfalls, overnight trade slackened to only 1.2 million on Tuesday.

The central bank was again not active in the currency market. It calculated the kuna midrates for Thursday weaker at 5.3838 to the dollar but stronger at 3.5553 against the mark. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
